title: Underpromotion: choose among four pieces
outcomes: Checks each of the four promotions instead of choosing by habit
Chooses the promoted piece that wins in a mixed set of endings
Says when the queen is the right choice, including when another piece wins as well

steps.text:
This lesson follows **Underpromotion: when a knight or rook beats the queen**. There you were told to underpromote. Now the position does not say, and the queen is often right.
For each of the four pieces ask: does the enemy king have a legal move (a queen can stalemate)? Does the piece give a check or fork that wins? Can it be captured, and does the win survive?

**The queen is correct** when it wins and the other pieces draw, or when another piece wins as well and adds nothing. **Another piece is correct** when the queen stalemates or loses to a reply it avoids.
In the next three positions only the promotion changes the result. The items state what was checked in the small endings.

steps.title: Same pawn, one change
steps.prompt: White to move in each position. Choose the promotion that wins. One change each time.
Name one promotion you rejected without checking in the silent positions. What would you have to ask to reject it properly: king moves, check, capture?
